Frequency the Elevation Recurs in Years
1. These graphs show that changes are expected in the water surface elevations of Amistad and Falcon Reservoirs under the two conditions of: 
Study A  The present condition, i.e., with the Falcon powerhouse but without the Amistad powerhouse (US side); and
Study B  the proposed condition, i.e., with the Falcon powerhouse and with the Amistad powerhouse (US side), but without Mexico's powerhouse at Amistad.
2. Explanation of Amistad Reservoir Graph. For that part of the reservoir between elevations 1117.0 and 1140.4 (the flood control storage pool), there will be no significant change in the elevation whether power facilities are added or not. For example, on average, the water surface can be expected to exceed elevation 1130 (11 feet or more into the flood storage) once every 45 years with or without power added to Amistad.
For that part of the reservoir below elevation 1117.0 (the conservation storage pool), there will be a change in operation that will result in a slight change in water surface elevations. For example, under present conditions (Study A), the surface will be below elevation 1020 (over 97 feet drawdown) about once every 37 to 38 years. Under the proposed condition (Study B), the surface will be below elevation 1020 about once every 27 years. Similarly, for present conditions, the surface will be lower than elevation 1040 every 10 years and lower than 1056 every 5 years. For the proposed conditions, the surface will be lower than elevation 1037 every 10 years and lower than 1053 every 5 years.
3. Explanation of Falcon Reservoir Graph. For that part of the reservoir between elevations 301.1 and 306.7 (the flood control pool), there will be a slight change. For example, under present conditions, the pool will be above elevation 305 once every 33 years, and under the proposed conditions it will reach that elevation once every 30 years.
For that part of the reservoir below elevation 301.1 (the conservation pool), the pool will be below elevation 250 once every 5 years under both present and proposed conditions. The frequency at which the surface will be below elevation 235 changes from 21 to 24 years for the two conditions. That is, the pool will be somewhat higher, on average, at Falcon under the proposed conditions than it is under present conditions.
4. Summary of Graphs on Plate IV-1. On average, Amistad would be unchanged in the flood control pool. On average, Amistad will change very little in operating the conservation storage, but about once every 20 years the difference will become significant, i.e., about 3 feet lower pool elevation.
On average, Falcon will be slightly higher in the flood pool about every 20 to 30 years. No significantly higher conservation pool can be expected for short frequencies, but drawdowns below elevation 240 will occur less frequently.
